title: Follow the Flow: On Information Flow Across Textual Tokens in Text-to-Image Models
role: Measures how often one item's meaning flows into another item's tokens at the text encoder output, and fixes word-sense leakage by patching in the item's context-free encoding; the text-encoder candidate for where leakage enters.
enters_evidence: Measurement: images generated from an item's contextual tokens alone (others set to pad outputs) show another item in 10.65% of 15,950 item pairs on FLUX-schnell; on 110 misread prompts the item's own contextual tokens already draw the wrong sense in 93% of cases.
changes: Replaces the misread item's text-encoder output tokens with the encoding of the item plus its local modifiers alone; all other tokens keep the full-prompt encoding; acts on the conditioning for every step (inferred).
training: Nothing trained for the patch; needs the item and its modifiers marked (GPT-4o / o3-mini-high item extraction in the paper); no boxes or masks. A separate one-layer redundancy classifier (25 epochs) is trained for the token-pruning result only.
model: FLUX-schnell and FLUX-dev (T5-XXL), SDXL-Turbo (CLIP), SANA 1.6B (Gemma); leakage fix tested on FLUX only
similar_subjects: No similar-subject split and no two-animal prompts; cross-item flow in 1,699 of 15,950 item pairs (10.65%) on FLUX-schnell.
which_pairs: Flow in about 11% of item pairs, often with no syntactic link; harmful flow concentrates on polysemous words; one-directional in causal encoders (SANA 17.45% vs FLUX 10.45%); 6.5% unintended after removing perceptually bound pairs; on Nano-Banana leakage rises to 42% when the item follows its cue.
when: not measured (text encoder output only, fixed across steps)
cost: Not printed; one extra text-encoder pass per patched item and no extra denoiser passes (inferred); whole study about 480 GPU hours on eight A100s.
headline: Patching cut prompts showing leakage on 110 curated polysemy prompts from 94% to 14% on FLUX-schnell (RAG-Diffusion 43%) and from 79% to 20% on FLUX-dev (RAG-Diffusion 39%); lower is better.
suggests: Text-side flow on SDXL's causal CLIP can only run from the earlier-named subject into the later one, so an order-swap test and a context-vs-isolated token drift predictor separate a text cause from an attention cause; CO3's single-subject encodings are the context-free tokens this fix patches in (inferred).

disagreements.claim: Brief: the literature calls one subject borrowing another subject's face, fur, beak or markings semantic leakage
